title: fix(god-mode): persist custom mechanic grants to resource_registry (issue #8320) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- God-Mode grants of custom check-triggered mechanics (e.g. "Conqueror's Spark," a `1d[level]` bonus, [#8320](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8320)) were narrative-only prose and drifted/were dropped on later turns.
- Fix extends the existing `player_character_data.resource_registry` store with `trigger_check_types`, `dice_expression`, and `apply_mode` fields instead of restructuring `features[]` — smaller blast radius, reuses proven backend-enforced infra (issue #7233).
- Prompt/schema-only change (`god_mode_instruction.md`, `dice_system_instruction.md`, `game_state_mechanics_appendix.md`, `game_state.schema.json`) plus additive server-side validation/warnings in `narrative_response_schema.py` (no new persistence logic, no state mutation).
- Real-LLM run (2/2 scenarios) confirms the model writes the intended structured entry when granted a custom mechanic via God Mode.

## Background

GH issue [#8320](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8320) / evidence PR [#8321](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8321): a user's custom "Conqueror's Spark" mechanic (`1d[level]` bonus to Persuasion/Insight checks), granted via God Mode at character creation, was written as narrative-only prose in `god_mode_response`. It was never persisted to any machine-parseable field. By turn 274 of campaign `xK3fp5XrV24oarIINTF7`, the LLM had to re-derive the mechanic from 270+ turns of prose, rolled `1d20+13` and silently dropped the expected `1d17` bonus. The user had to keep re-asserting the rule every turn.

Static-evidence greps (from issue #8320) confirmed zero canonical representation: `player_character_data.features[]` contained the grant only as a plain string, with no trigger, formula, or apply-mode data anywhere.

## Goals

- Give the LLM a structured place to persist a check-triggered custom mechanic at grant time, so it does not need to re-derive the rule from narrative prose on every later turn.
- Stay within this repo's ZFC / root-cause-first policy: the model decides the mechanic; the server only persists, validates, and renders it. No backend regex/heuristic parsing of narrative text.
- Minimize blast radius: reuse existing, already-shipped machinery rather than inventing a new schema.

## Tenets

**Design Decision:** rev-ew20b — see `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_mechanics_appendix.md` for the extended `ResourceEntry` field docs (`trigger_check_types`, `dice_expression`, `apply_mode`) that implement this decision.

- **Root-cause-first**: fix the prompt contract, not a backend adjuster/inference layer.
- **Reuse over invention**: `player_character_data.resource_registry` (issue #7233) already exists precisely for "LLM-defined resource: D&D 5e class features, custom... charges, or anything else the campaign introduces," is already backend-enforced (clamp, reset-on-rest) and already rendered in the session header. Extending it is smaller and safer than restructuring `features[]` from `List[str]` to `List[Dict]` campaign-wide (which would break an invariant several other prompts rely on).
- **Validation-only backend**: the added `narrative_response_schema.py` checks (below) only validate and warn — no new state mutation, inference, or narrative parsing.

## High-level description

Two design options were considered:
- **(A) Extend `resource_registry`** with `trigger_check_types[]`, `dice_expression`, `apply_mode` fields (chosen).
- (B) Restructure `player_character_data.features[]` from `List[str]` to `List[Dict]` (rejected — bigger blast radius, breaks an existing invariant).

Changes:
- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`: new **Custom Mechanic Grant Invariant (MANDATORY, issue #8320)** — any check-triggered custom mechanic grant must also write a `resource_registry` entry with the new fields, alongside the existing narrative response. Includes a full worked JSON example using "The Conqueror's Spark".
- `mvp_site/prompts/dice_system_instruction.md` + `mvp_site/prompts/shared/dice_notation_contract.md`: extends the existing narrative-only "separate roll" pattern (Bardic Inspiration / Sneak Attack / Divine Smite) into a **mandatory rule**: scan `resource_registry` for entries whose `trigger_check_types` match the current check, resolve `1d[level]` at roll time, and roll the `dice_expression` as an extra roll (add or reroll per `apply_mode`), reporting `mechanics.combined_total` and decrementing limited-use entries.
- `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_mechanics_appendix.md` + `mvp_site/schemas/game_state.schema.json`: document the 3 new optional `ResourceEntry` fields (`dependentRequired` in JSON Schema — all three travel together or none). `additionalProperties: true` was already set, so this is documentation plus a stricter conditional constraint, not a breaking schema change.

## Production Code Changes

- **`mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`** (`_validate_resource_registry`): before → the function validated `current`/`max`/`reset_trigger`/`category` only. Now → it also validates that `trigger_check_types`/`dice_expression`/`apply_mode` appear together (all three or none), that `trigger_check_types` is a non-empty list of non-empty strings, `dice_expression` is a non-empty string, and `apply_mode` is `"add"` or `"reroll"`. Why → the model's own `resource_registry` writes need a validation backstop consistent with this repo's "warnings only, no assertions/retries/default content" error-handling philosophy — bad LLM output surfaces as a warning, it does not silently corrupt game state.
- **`mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`** (`action_resolution.mechanics.combined_total`): added a type-check warning when `mechanics.combined_total` is present but non-numeric, since the new dice-notation contract introduces this field for add/reroll bonus totals. Warning-only, matches existing `_warn_on_unclean_action_resolution_dice` pattern in the same class.
- No new persistence logic, no narrative-text parsing, no server-computed game decisions — `_canonicalize_resource_registry_in_place` (`mvp_site/game_state.py:1255`) already passed through unknown dict fields untouched before this PR and continues to do so; the validation added here only warns.

## Test Changes

- **New**: `mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization.py` — RED→GREEN prompt-contract tests asserting `god_mode_instruction.md` and `dice_system_instruction.md` contain the new required language.
- **New**: `testing_mcp/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py` — real local-server + real-LLM scenario granting "The Conqueror's Spark" via God Mode and asserting the structured `resource_registry` entry appears with the correct trigger/formula/mode fields.
- **Extended**: `mvp_site/tests/test_resource_registry.py` — additional coverage for the new `_validate_resource_registry` mechanic-field checks (paired-field requirement, type/enum validation).

## Testing

### Unit / prompt-contract (RED → GREEN)

`mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization.py` — 2 tests asserting `god_mode_instruction.md` and `dice_system_instruction.md` contain the new required language. Confirmed RED (failing) against `origin/main` before the fix, GREEN after.

### Regression

Ran all 6 test files referencing the 3 edited prompt files (`test_agents.py`, `test_compression_lever1.py`, `test_dice_prompt_advantage_disadvantage.py`, `test_god_mode_prompt_time_rules.py`, `test_god_mode_stale_combat_cleanup.py`, `test_prompts.py`) plus `test_resource_registry.py` and `test_god_mode_response_field.py`: **526 passed, 3 skipped, 0 new failures.** 3 pre-existing failures in `test_god_mode_prompt_level_signal_rule.py` confirmed via `git stash` to already exist on `origin/main` HEAD `007f7d3fde`, unrelated to this change.

### Real LLM (testing_mcp, real Gemini API)

`testing_mcp/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py`: real local MCP server + real `gemini-3-flash-preview` call (`AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` — AGY needs interactive TTY auth refresh unavailable in this harness, so this uses the documented Gemini-API fallback path, matching sibling test `test_resource_registry_no_rest_refresh_real_llm.py`). Grants "The Conqueror's Spark" via God Mode, then asserts a structured `resource_registry` entry appears.

**Result: 2/2 scenarios PASSED.** The real model produced exactly the intended structure:

```json
"conquerors_spark": {
  "trigger_check_types": ["persuasion", "insight"],
```

The model's own `god_mode_response` text confirmed it followed the new contract: *"This feature has been integrated into the character's `resource_registry` with automated trigger logic... Trigger: Any Persuasion or Insight skill check. Effect: Automatically adds 1d17... to the final roll total."*

## Known Limitations

- This PR's real-LLM evidence covers **grant-time persistence** (confirmed). It does not include a second real-LLM scenario proving the dice-roll rubric change (`dice_system_instruction.md`) actually causes the model to roll the bonus on a *later* matching check turn in a long-running campaign — that would require a longer multi-turn real-LLM scenario. The RED/GREEN prompt-contract test does cover that instruction's text.
- Does not touch `player_character_data.features[]` (still `List[str]`) — narrative-only features are unaffected; only check-triggered custom mechanics need the new registry fields.

comments.text:
Sidekick evaluation of #179 disposition (requested by main after codex
BLOCK_MERGE, 2026-07-07): recommend CLOSE #179 as superseded, salvage only
the doc text as a fresh small PR. Evidence:

1. Code is genuinely superseded, not just stale. #179's `daemon/scripts/
   ready-scheduler.sh` + `daemon/factory-af-tick.sh` wiring duplicates a
   READY transition the Rust daemon already performs in-process:
   daemon/src/tick.rs:1178-1207 runs `verifier::assess(...)` every tick and
   sets `overlay.state = OverlayState::Ready` directly when
   `report.all_green`. Confirmed in daemon/src/verifier.rs:56-57:
   `all_green` is `true` only when **every** one of the 7 gates is `Green` —
   a single `Unknown` gate forces `all_green=false`. #179's shell scheduler
   (per main's codex review + PR body) treats "no red AND all 7 accounted
   for (green OR unknown)" as READY-sufficient — that is a real semantic
   regression vs. the Rust path, not a stylistic difference: it would let a
   bead reach READY with an Unknown (not confirmed-green) gate, which the
   Rust verifier explicitly refuses to do. Merging #179's shell writer would
   create two READY writers with two different (and conflicting)
   correctness bars.
2. #179's stated justification is stale. Its PR body argues no-merge-side-
   effect stance is needed because "gate 6 (/er) has no automated runner
   (bead jleechan-qqq still open)" — jleechan-qqq is actually CLOSED,
   merged via PR #178 (`er_runner.rs`, wired into tick.rs). The premise for
   why #179 exists at all no longer holds.
3. The doc fix IS still a real, unaddressed gap. #179 also edits
   docs/auto-factory-daemon-spec.md §4.2.8, replacing "Merge: never." with
   reconciliation language resolving the "Merge: never" (§4.2.8) vs "must
   attempt merge" (cutover X4) contradiction. Checked current main
   (docs/auto-factory-daemon-spec.md:273) — it STILL says "Merge: never."
   with no reconciliation. This bead (s3c) is exactly about that
   contradiction and is not resolved by anything else that landed today.

Recommendation: close #179 (superseded — the code path is a correctness
regression, not just redundant), then land a small doc-only follow-up PR
against current main that:
  - Replaces the "Merge: never." line in §4.2.8 with reconciliation text
    describing the ACTUAL current mechanism: the Rust daemon's in-process
    READY transition (tick.rs:1178-1207 / verifier.rs all_green, strict
    Unknown-forces-false), not #179's shell-script description (which
    encodes the weaker unknown-tolerant policy and should NOT be copied
    verbatim).
  - Notes merge authority itself remains operator/human (or a future
    7-green-enforcing automation) — same "no merge side effect" tenet
    #179 argued for, just attributed to the mechanism that's actually
    live in main.
This keeps s3c's scope (resolve the spec contradiction) but drops the
shell-script implementation entirely.

comments.text:
Sidekick scoping pass (2026-07-07): design is now concrete but implementation
is BLOCKED-BY-190 (PR #190 not yet merged as of this comment) and needs one
explicit behavioral confirmation before a coder subagent touches it.

Code trace (against origin/main @ 1aa0a48, pre-#190):
- Sessions trait: daemon/src/tools.rs:211 `fn attach(&self, branch: &str, bead_id: &str)`
- Production impl currently unconditionally errors:
  daemon/src/adapters.rs:917 `Err(DaemonError::Config("attach is disabled/unimplemented"))`
- Call site: daemon/src/reroll.rs:157 — reroll calls `sessions.attach(branch,
  bead_id)` to find the CURRENTLY RUNNING session for `bead.branch`, then
  stops it (line 166) and waits for quiescence, THEN (line 220-225)
  unconditionally fabricates a fresh `factory/{bead_id}-r{attempt}` branch
  and closes the old PR (line 242-245) — for EVERY reroll, factory-owned or
  not.
- PR #190 (unmerged) adds `bead.branch = Some(adopted.head_ref_name.clone())`
  for adopted external PRs (see intake::normalize_labeled_prs in the diff) —
  so after #190 lands, `bead.branch` can legitimately hold either a
  factory-fabricated branch (`factory/<id>-rN`) or an external contributor's
  own branch name. Reroll's step-5 fabrication does not distinguish these:
  it will always create a new `factory/...` branch and close the PR on ANY
  reroll, which for an adopted PR means abandoning the contributor's real

title: daemon repeatedly re-attempts create_bead for an already-tracked external ref despite unpaginated dedup query showing it present
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-07 during /af E2E canary (goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/). Even AFTER PR #191's pagination fix was merged, deployed, and confirmed present in the running binary (verified via `strings daemon/target/release/daemon | grep "refusing partial"` — the fail-closed string IS compiled in), the daemon STILL repeatedly failed with:

  tool br failed (rc=7): Error: Configuration error: External reference 'jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#8227' already exists on issue jleechan-vj89

...for many consecutive ticks (growing backoff 10s->20s->40s->80s->160s->300s cap), even though a direct, unpaginated query run manually during the same window confirms the ref IS present and correctly discoverable:

  br list --status open --json --limit 0 | jq shows jleechan-vj89 with external_ref="jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#8227"

Sequence observed:
1. Fresh issue #8227 created + labeled factory (no prior history, first-ever adoption).
2. Daemon's intake::normalize() (daemon/src/intake.rs:56-95) correctly created bead jleechan-vj89 for it (confirmed via sqlite ~/.dark-factory/daemon-cxdb.sqlite bead_overlay row, state=QUEUED, pr_number=8227).
3. Bead got a branch assigned (factory/jleechan-vj89-r1) via dispatch/routing logic later in the same tick (run_slow_tier, tick.rs:556+).
4. Dispatch's `ao spawn` call failed (rc=1) because the Agent Orchestrator daemon itself was not running on this host ("AO is not running — lifecycle polling is inactive. Run `ao start` before spawning sessions") — a SEPARATE operational gap, not a code bug (mitigated live by running `ao start`).
5. On SUBSEQUENT ticks, intake::normalize() began repeatedly failing on THE SAME #8227 ref with "already exists" — i.e., the known_refs dedup check (intake.rs:72, `if known_refs.contains(&issue.external_ref) { continue; }`) is NOT catching a ref that objectively exists per a manual `br list --limit 0` check run in the same window.

This is NOT the original jleechan-v09l pagination bug (fixed, confirmed compiled in) and is a DIFFERENT, deeper idempotency gap — possibly: a stale/separate cache path for fetch_all_external_refs() despite its own --limit 0 usage, a race between the sqlite state-store write and the next tick's br list read (e.g., WAL checkpoint delay), or a subtle mismatch in how external_ref strings are compared. Also related: jleechan-uinw (missing per-candidate isolation in intake::normalize's loop) makes this WORSE since one bad candidate blocks the whole batch every tick, but that's a separate, already-filed gap.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproduce with a minimal test: create a bead via intake::normalize() for a fresh external ref, then run a SECOND intake::normalize() call (or full tick) immediately after and confirm it does NOT attempt create_bead again for the same ref.
- If the repro requires a live daemon (not just unit-level), instrument fetch_all_external_refs() with telemetry logging its returned set size + whether the specific ref is present, to compare against a manual `br list --limit 0` at the same instant.
- Fix root cause; add a regression test that would have caught this (a bead created in tick N must be excluded from create_bead candidates in tick N+1 without requiring a process restart).
notes: Root cause: known_refs bulk snapshot read in intake::normalize/normalize_labeled_prs races with br create's own write-time uniqueness check. Fix: PR jleechanorg/dark-factory#192 catches the rc=7 'already exists' error and treats it as idempotent skip instead of a tick-killing transient error. Live daemon rebuilt+restarted with fix; zero errors since restart; jleechan-vj89 QUEUED (not erroring) awaiting dispatch slot.

title: daemon intake::normalize aborts entire batch on first bad candidate — no per-candidate isolation
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-07 during /af E2E canary testing: installed the real systemd daemon on main (ed52665) pointed at jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai, and it got stuck retrying a single stale duplicate candidate (issue #8164 / bead jleechan-fk9q) forever with growing backoff.

Root cause of the stuck state itself is the fetch_all_external_refs() pagination truncation (tracked separately, fixed by PR #191). But a SEPARATE, independent gap: daemon/src/intake.rs:56-95 normalize() loops over ALL factory-labeled issues in one function, and daemon/src/tick.rs:639 calls it with `?` (single-shot propagation). If create_bead() (intake.rs:86) errors for ANY one issue in the batch, the whole normalize() call returns Err immediately — meaning any OTHER genuinely-new labeled issue later in that same iteration order never gets created that slow-tier tick either. This differs from the active-overlay dispatch loop (tick.rs:213), which already has explicit per-item error isolation via `continue` (see "jleechan-qdw: per-overlay isolation" comment at tick.rs:215) — that pattern should be applied to intake::normalize's loop too.

Acceptance criteria:
- intake::normalize's for-loop should catch a per-issue error (e.g. create_bead failing on an unexpected duplicate, or any other single-issue failure), record/emit telemetry for that issue, and continue to the next issue rather than propagating via `?` and aborting the whole batch.
- Add a regression test: 2 labeled issues where the first hits an error (e.g. simulated create_bead failure) and the second is legitimately new — assert the second issue still gets a bead created in the same call.
- Consider whether normalize_labeled_prs (tick.rs:563, the PR-adoption sibling) has the same gap and needs the same fix.

title: [agento] feat(ux): genre-first campaign wizard with 3-module previews (issue #7966) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
Beads: none

## Summary

Replaces the binary `Custom vs Dragon Knight` campaign wizard with a **genre-first picker**: 4 genre tabs × 3 module cards = 12 starter campaigns with 1-line taglines. Issue [#7966](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7966) — 7/8 real users bounced off the default Dragon Knight template because the only alternative was a blank `Custom` form. The fix surfaces `Build Your Own` as a top-level module rather than burying it, and removes the silent first-card-highlight that misled users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected on first paint.

## Production Code Changes

| Area | Before | Now | Why |
|------|--------|-----|-----|
| `CampaignWizard.MODULE_CATALOG` | Did not exist; only `mvp_site/campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` was reachable from the wizard | 4 genres × 3 modules each (12 starters); static getter so it can reference `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` declared further down the class | Gives users a real choice instead of one rich prefill + one blank form (87.5% bounced off DK) |
| `generateWizardHTML()` step 1 | Binary radio set (`Custom` / `Dragon Knight`) only | Adds `.genre-picker` + `.module-grid` alongside the legacy `.campaign-type-card` block | Genre-first picker is the new UX; legacy markup stays for the SHA-256 fast-path + back-compat |
| `handleModuleSelect(moduleEntry)` | Did not exist | New method that seeds `title` / `character` / `setting` / `description` inputs from a module and marks the card `.active`; routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio so `handleCampaignTypeChange` keeps locking description + preloading the Arion avatar | Wires module selection to the existing wizard state machine without duplicating description-lock or preview-update logic |
| `renderModulesForGenre(genreKey)` | Did not exist | Re-renders `.module-grid` when a genre tab is clicked | Genre tabs drive module content |
| First-paint module card | Rendered with `${idx === 0 ? 'active' : ''}` so Dragon Knight was visually highlighted while `selectedCampaignType` stayed `'custom'` (state mismatch) | No module card renders with `active` on first paint — only an explicit user click sets the class via `handleModuleSelect` | CodeRabbit P2 fix: stop misleading users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected |

**Files changed:**

- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/js/campaign-wizard.js` (+302 / -3) — adds `MODULE_CATALOG`, `handleModuleSelect`, `renderModulesForGenre`, drops auto-highlight
- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (+268 / new) — 8 lock-in tests
- `docs/evidence/pr-8006/*.png` (+5 / new) — visual evidence (5 screenshots, 537 KB)

**No backend changes.** The Dragon Knight SHA-256 fast-path in `campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` keeps matching because `handleModuleSelect` routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio and seeds the canonical `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` verbatim. Verified via `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_frontend_backend_sync.py` (1/1) and `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_fastpath_evidence.py` (8/8).

## Test Changes

- **NEW** `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (8 tests):
  1. `MODULE_CATALOG` exposes ≥ 4 genres
  2. Every genre has ≥ 3 modules with `title` + `tagline` + `character` + `setting` + `description`
  3. Dragon Knight is reachable as a module under the Fantasy genre AND its description equals `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` (locks the SHA-256 fast-path)
  4. Custom / Build Your Own is surfaced as a top-level module
  5. `.genre-picker` and `.module-grid` are present in the wizard HTML
  6. Legacy `.campaign-type-card` markup preserved for back-compat
  7. **No module card renders with `active` on first paint** (CodeRabbit P2 regression lock — guards against re-introducing the silent Dragon Knight default)
  8. `handleModuleSelect()` fills all four wizard inputs from a module entry
- No changes to existing test files. Full wizard suite: **31/31 pass** (was 30/30, +1 new).

## Known Limitations

- **Visual proof is rendered against a static HTML fixture, not the live preview server.** The preview deployment requires real Firebase auth, and `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS` only works on `localhost` per `mvp_site/main.py:1962-1967`. The `wizard_render.html` fixture mirrors the exact markup emitted by `generateWizardHTML()` and uses the actual `MODULE_CATALOG` data, so the screenshots are byte-faithful representations of the new wizard. Drive against the live preview server manually if you want to confirm the click handlers wire up the same way.
- **Metrics for the 7-day bounce-rate review are out of scope** for this PR and tracked in issue [#7967](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7967).
- **Auto-testing-ui pipeline is not invoked here.** A future PR could add `mvp_site/testing_ui/test_campaign_wizard_genre_picker.py` mirroring `test_campaign_wizard_screenshots.py`; this PR focuses on the visible UX fix.

## Unit Test Evidence

```
$ node --test mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_*.test.js
…
1..31
# tests 31
# suites 0
# pass 31
# fail 0
# cancelled 0
# skipped 0
# todo 0
# duration_ms 119.305208
```

(Full output: `/tmp/pr8006_evidence/wizard_tests_output.txt` — 31/31 pass, including the new test 7 that locks the no-auto-highlight behavior.)

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Five screenshots, captured via Playwright headless against the static-render fixture, plus a composite animated GIF that walks through all five states. All committed to the repo and reachable via raw.githubusercontent.com so the URLs are stable even after the PR is merged:

**Animated walkthrough (all 5 states in one):**
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/feat/7966-campaign-picker-drive-to-green-pr-brief-tmp-worldarchi/docs/evidence/pr-8006/wizard_walkthrough.gif

**Individual states:**
- Initial paint — **no module card is highlighted** (the CodeRabbit P2 fix):
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/feat/7966-campaign-picker-drive-to-green-pr-brief-tmp-worldarchi/docs/evidence/pr-8006/01_initial_paint_no_active.png

## Evidence

> **Campaign wizard step 1** now leads with a **genre-first picker** (four genres × three module cards) instead of only surfacing Custom vs Dragon Knight. New **`MODULE_CATALOG`**, **`handleModuleSelect`**, and **`renderModulesForGenre`** seed title/character/setting/description from the chosen starter; Dragon Knight still goes through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio and canonical description so the backend SHA-256 fast-path is unchanged. title: P0: daemon tick dies fatally — br list pagination truncates external-ref dedup at 50
description: Repro: ./daemon/target/release/daemon --once -> 'fatal: tool br failed (rc=7): External reference jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#8164 already exists on issue jleechan-fk9q'. Root cause: br list --json defaults to limit 50 (130 open beads, has_more:true); fetch_all_external_refs (daemon/src/adapters.rs:41) parses only page 1, so refs on later pages are invisible to dedup; daemon re-creates bead for an already-tracked GH issue; br rc=7 is treated as fatal, killing the entire tick. /af cannot complete one tick. Fix: pass --limit 0 to both br list calls + regression test; optionally treat 'already exists' create errors as adopt-existing instead of fatal. Evidence: /tmp/dark-factory/sidekick/af-e2e/evidence/af-probe-tick1/tick-once.log

CLOSED 2026-07-07: fixed by PR #191 (merged 5e4c876) — daemon/src/adapters.rs fetch_all_external_refs()
now uses `br list --limit 0` (unlimited) for both open+closed status, with fail-closed truncation
detection in parse_external_refs_from_br_list (has_more=true -> Err rather than silent partial dedup
set). Independently adversarially verified PASS (mutation-tested against live 131+ issue dataset).

Further hardened by PR #192 (merged 1bbbc8f) which fixed a related TOCTOU race: even with the
--limit 0 fix, a bulk known_refs snapshot could still miss a ref created between the snapshot read and
the create_bead call under concurrent write contention. #192 makes create_bead's own "already exists"
rejection the authoritative idempotency backstop (catches the error at the call site, treats as skip)
instead of relying solely on the upfront snapshot. Both fixes were live-reproduced and verified during
the 2026-07-07 /af E2E canary session (see goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/, STATE.md at
/tmp/dark-factory/sidekick/af-e2e/STATE.md) — the daemon was observed getting genuinely stuck on this
exact bug class against real production state, then confirmed unstuck after both fixes landed.

description:
Beads: rev-onrvh

## Summary

- Investigated bead `rev-onrvh` (fleet-wide Green Gate `conclusion=cancelled` on 20+/22 open PRs) with live `gh api` data and **disproved** the `workflow_call`/concurrency-group-collision theory for `green-gate.yml` — the workflow has no `workflow_call:` trigger and its group key is already correctly per-PR-scoped (PR #8231 already fixed `cancel-in-progress` on `main`).
- Live data instead shows the `cancelled` conclusions time-clustered across unrelated PRs (independent of each PR's own push time) — the signature of an external bulk-cancel/queue-drain sweep, not a workflow-YAML bug. Documented this diagnosis inline in `green-gate.yml` so it isn't re-investigated as the same already-fixed theory.
- Fixed the second, confirmed, in-repo bug: `.claude/skills/pr-green-definition.md`'s canonical gate-log grep matched literal unreached `echo "GATE-N ..."` YAML source text, producing false PASS/FAIL noise.

## Production Code Changes

title: daemon has no preflight check for AO orchestrator availability before ao spawn
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-07 during /af E2E canary (goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/). After a fresh systemd daemon install, the daemon correctly created a bead and assigned a branch for a fresh candidate, then attempted `ao spawn` to dispatch a worker session — which failed with:

  tool ao spawn failed (rc=1): ... ✗ AO is not running — lifecycle polling is inactive. Run `ao start` before spawning sessions so they get CI/review routing and state advancement.

This is a real operational gap: the daemon has no preflight check that Agent Orchestrator itself is running before attempting to spawn a session. On a freshly-booted host (e.g. after a reboot, or a fresh systemd daemon install like this one), AO may not be running yet, and the daemon's dispatch step just fails with a generic transient-tool error indistinguishable from other `ao spawn` failures, rather than a clear "AO is down" signal that could trigger a distinct remediation path (e.g. attempt `ao start` itself, or escalate distinctly from a normal spawn failure).

Worked around live via manually running `ao start` in the background.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a preflight check (e.g. `ao status` or equivalent) at daemon startup and/or before each dispatch attempt, distinguishing "AO not running" from other spawn failures.
- Decide and implement a remediation policy: should the daemon attempt to start AO itself (if that's safe/idempotent), or just escalate distinctly (e.g. a specific telemetry event / PR comment) so an operator knows to run `ao start` rather than debugging a generic transient tool error?
- Add a test simulating AO-not-running and asserting the distinct signal/remediation path fires.

title: fix(world_logic): atomically clear level-up modal lock on level-up completion (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Beads: rev-c5lc4 (residual: pcd.custom_campaign_state mirror sync)

Fix the level-up modal-lock clearing flow: when `custom_campaign_state.level_up_complete=True` on a turn, `mvp_site/world_logic.py:_persist_turn_to_firestore` now **pops** `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` from `custom_campaign_state` BEFORE the canonical `update_campaign_game_state` batch write, so the lock flags are absent from the Firestore subdoc on the next read.

## Background

PRs #8123, #8124, #8125, #8177 all touched this same flow in different files. The real bug was three-fold:

1. **Wrong document** (PR #8123 path): the original code wrote `custom_state.level_up_*` keys on the CAMPAIGN document, but production reads `level_up_in_progress` / `level_up_pending` from `game_states/current_state.custom_campaign_state` (the game_state subdoc). The cross-doc routing never reached the right place.

2. **Wrong sentinel** (an earlier draft of this PR): `DELETE_TOKEN` in this codebase is an app-level string sentinel `"__DELETE__"` used by the `update_state_with_changes` dispatch path (which calls `_handle_delete_token` and translates it to a `del` on the dict). `update_campaign_game_state` calls `game_state_ref.set(game_state_update)` directly — `set()` does NOT translate `DELETE_TOKEN`, so writing that string persisted as a literal value, not a delete. Fixed by using `dict.pop()` (omit the key entirely from the dict that `set()` receives; omitted keys stay deleted on the Firestore side).

3. **No live-mode /es evidence**: previous PRs in this family only had unit tests. This PR adds `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` driving the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini-powered campaign + real Firestore, asserting both flags are absent after a turn that sets `level_up_complete=True`.

## Goals

- Make level-up completion actually clear the modal lock in Firestore.
- Use the canonical in-place `game_state_ref.set()` path; no new cross-doc helper needed.
- Keep the change set minimal — `pop()` is the canonical "delete a field from the next set()" pattern.
- Provide /es real-mode evidence per `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` evidence standards.

## High-level description

Replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state(user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict)` call inside `_persist_turn_to_firestore` with:

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

`game_state_ref.set()` is a full doc replacement, so popping the keys omits them from the next read.

## Production Code Changes

### Before

```python
firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
    user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
)
```

### After

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

### Why

`update_campaign_game_state` writes via `game_state_ref.set()`, which replaces the entire subdoc. Omitting the keys from the dict that's passed in leaves them absent in Firestore on the next read — the canonical "delete a field" pattern for `set()`. The cross-doc path PR #8123 tried was unnecessary; the canonical home of these flags has been `custom_campaign_state` all along.

## Test Changes

### Added (in `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994`)

`TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`:
- `test_level_up_completed_pops_lock_flags_before_write` — RED pre-fix (the write committed but the flags stayed True); GREEN post-fix (asserts both flags are absent from the dict passed to `update_campaign_game_state`).
- `test_no_level_up_completed_leaves_lock_flags_untouched` — confirms the non-completed path passes the dict through unchanged (no regression on the existing flow).

### Added (real-mode /es in `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py`)

Drives the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini + real Firestore campaign. Builds a game_state dict with all three flags set, runs the persist function, then reads back via `get_game_state` and asserts both lock flags are absent from the top-level `custom_campaign_state`.

## Verification

## Unit Test Evidence

## Real LLM Evidence

The /es test used real Gemini 3 Flash in `create_campaign` (canonical wizard setup). Live `_persist_turn_to_firestore` was driven by the test directly — `gemini_http_request_responses.jsonl` shows the full LLM turn traces.

## Evidence

**Gist (canonical bundle):** https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/5db70e03f0f59a7cdf6fadf822469bb5

The /es evidence bundle at `/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/codex_pr7236-merge-main/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear/iteration_003/` proves:
- Both `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` are absent (not the literal `"__DELETE__"` string, not `False`, but truly omitted) from `top-level custom_campaign_state` AFTER `_persist_turn_to_firestore` runs with `level_up_complete=True`.
- `player_character_data.level` was correctly persisted to 2 from our seed (proves the canonical write reached Firestore).

## Known Limitations

1. **Sister PRs #8123 / #8124 / #8125** touch the same flow in orthogonal paths:
   - #8123 (BROKEN: calls an undefined helper): recommend close with `superseded-by-#8177` comment.
   - #8124 (touch `llm_service.py`, strips legacy level-up flags): orthogonal; flag for separate review.
   - #8125 (touch `agents.py`): orthogonal; flag for separate review.

2. **Branch is 57 commits behind `main`** because this branch tracks the PR #8149 merge-main lane. CI will run against current `main` HEAD when this merges; the fix is local to `world_logic.py` and unrelated to the 57-commit delta, so risk is low.

3. **`player_character_data.custom_campaign_state.level_up_in_progress` may still appear True** after a single persist turn — that's an auto-derived mirror copy written by `update_state_with_changes`'s deep-merge from a different state_updates path; the canonical home (top-level `custom_campaign_state`) is what `_persist_turn_to_firestore` writes, and that's where the modal-lock guards read from. Confirmed by `agent_prompts.py` and `_level_up_*` checks in `agents.py:3411` and `game_state.py:1612` — they all read from the canonical top-level location.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/world_logic.py:5775-5803` — replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state` call with the `level_up_completed` branch.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994` — new class `TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`.
- `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` — new file, 193 LOC.

## bead

Filed `rev-fix-pr-8162-scope` (now closed by previous session work) and a new guard bead in this session's `/ms` capture: do not re-introduce the `custom_state.*` campaign-side routing path.


## Design Doc
DESIGN DOC: N/A

This PR is a small, surgical backend bugfix. The change is purely a fix to existing logic - it does not introduce a new feature, change the API surface, modify the data model, or alter the LLM contract.

- **Symptom**: level_up_complete=True did not clear modal-lock flags.
- **Root cause**: reset_resource_registry_in_place() ran AFTER update_campaign_game_state(), and a new write would have over-written the cleared values. The fix is to mutate the dict BEFORE the canonical write, so set() replaces the whole subdoc with the cleared values.
- **Decision**: pop() (not DELETE_TOKEN) because update_campaign_game_state() does not translate DELETE_TOKEN; only mutate-in-place before the write works.
- **Asymmetry**: long_rest resets both long_rest AND short_rest triggers per 5e SRD (Warlock spell slots, monk ki, fighter superiority dice all reset on long rest); short_rest only resets short_rest triggers.

No design doc needed for a 6-line fix to existing logic.

title: feat(smoke): dark-factory end-to-end smoke harness (TDD) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Adds a deterministic, hermetic smoke harness for the dark-factory pipeline runner plus a TDD test suite that locks the contract. The harness shells out to the real dark-factory binary on PATH, parses its JSON envelope, and exposes a SmokeResult dataclass so CI and scripts can assert on final_outcome, trace, evidence_bundle, and events.jsonl without writing shell glue.

- New harness: scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py
  - run_smoke(pipeline_text, workdir, goal, *, backend="echo", max_steps=10) programmatic API
  - preflight(pipeline_text, workdir) programmatic API
  - CLI entry points: --self-test and --pipeline <dot>
- New TDD test suite: scripts/tests/test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py
  - 7 unittest cases covering preflight validation, broken-pipeline diagnostics, harness module existence, echo-backend end-to-end execution (minimal + codergen), and evidence-bundle materialisation
- Default backend is echo so the smoke run is hermetic (no real LLM calls); CI can override via the backend parameter

## Production Code Changes

| File | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py | n/a (new) | Deterministic dark-factory smoke harness with run_smoke() / preflight() APIs and CLI entry points | Operators and CI need a hermetic end-to-end probe of the dark-factory runner without paying for real LLM calls |
| scripts/tests/test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py | n/a (new) | TDD contract: 7 unittest cases pinning the harness behaviour | Lock in the harness API so future refactors cannot silently regress preflight, end-to-end run, or evidence materialisation |

## Test Changes

| File | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| scripts/tests/test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py | 0 tests | 7 unittest cases (3.95s wall clock, no LLM) | TDD: RED captured the missing harness, GREEN captured the passing contract |

## Known Limitations

- The harness shells out to the locally-installed dark-factory binary; if PATH does not include dark-factory, all tests are skipped (@unittest.skipUnless) rather than failing.
- The default echo backend only exercises the pipeline engine and node visit ordering; it does not prove semantic correctness of any specific slash-command gate. Operators who need gate-level coverage should run a real backend in addition.

## User Stories

- Operator wants a fast, hermetic probe to verify the dark-factory runner is healthy after a release. Story: runs `python3 scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py --self-test`; gets exit 0 plus visible OK in <2s without paying for LLM tokens.
- CI author wants a unittest-callable smoke test that does not flake on missing secrets. Story: runs `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke`; gets deterministic pass/fail because echo backend never touches an external API.

## TDD Cycle

| Phase | Command | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| RED | python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke (before harness existed) | 5 of 7 tests failed with FileNotFoundError on dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py and ModuleNotFoundError on the run_smoke import |
| GREEN | python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke | 7 of 7 tests pass in 3.95s |

RED proof captured in red_phase_output.txt inside the evidence bundle.

## Evidence

- Evidence bundle: /tmp/worldarchitect.ai/feat_feat-auto-factory-end-to-end-smoke-test-jleechanorg-worldar/dark_factory_e2e_smoke/latest/
  - test_output.txt - verbose unittest output (7 tests, all pass)
  - self_test_output.txt - --self-test CLI output (1 test, passes)
  - preflight_real_pipeline.txt - --pipeline dark-factory/pipelines/pr_gates_split_cs.dot (status=pass)
  - red_phase_output.txt - initial RED run before harness existed
  - MANIFEST.md / manifest.json - bundle metadata
- HEAD SHA: 3ca2d49e616183c781c60027ca506c99d2024fca
- Branch: feat/feat-auto-factory-end-to-end-smoke-test-jleechanorg-worldarc

## Reproduction

```bash
# Run the TDD contract
python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke -v

# Run the embedded self-test via CLI
python3 scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py --self-test

# Preflight a real pipeline from this repo
python3 scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py --pipeline dark-factory/pipelines/pr_gates_split_cs.dot
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> New scripts and tests only; no production app paths changed, and the echo backend avoids external LLM or secret dependencies.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **hermetic CI smoke path** for the dark-factory pipeline runner: a new harness shells out to the local `dark-factory` CLI, uses the default **`echo`** backend (no real LLM calls), and returns structured **`SmokeResult`** data (outcome, trace, evidence paths) from parsed JSON.
> 
> **`scripts/dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py`** adds `run_smoke()` and `preflight()`, trace parsing that **skips non-dict trace entries**, and a CLI that defaults to an embedded self-test, with optional `--self-test` and `--pipeline` preflight for a `.dot` file.
> 
> **`scripts/tests/test_dark_factory_e2e_smoke.py`** locks the contract: preflight pass/fail on minimal vs broken pipelines, module/API presence, echo-backed e2e runs (minimal and codergen graphs), evidence bundle / `events.jsonl` materialization, and pure-unit tests for `_parse_trace`. CLI-dependent cases **skip** when `dark-factory` is not on `$PATH`.

title: execute_adopted's duplicate-spawn guard fails OPEN (not closed) when attach()'s ao status --json call itself errors
description: Prereq #1 re-validation (post-#204/#209) found: daemon/src/reroll.rs's execute_adopted duplicate-spawn guard uses 'if let Ok(existing_session) = attach(...)' -- if ao status --json itself fails or times out (a transient infra error, distinct from 'no session found for this branch'), attach() returns Err, which the if-let treats identically to 'no existing session' and falls through to spawn a NEW session anyway -- bypassing the duplicate-spawn guard exactly when it's least trustworthy (can't verify there's no existing session, so optimistically assumes there isn't). Contrast: the non-adopted reroll path (reroll.rs:232) treats ANY attach() Err as HumanHeld (fail-safe/fail-closed). The adopted path does not have the same fail-closed behavior. Recommend: park HumanHeld on attach() Err in execute_adopted too (matching the non-adopted path's convention), or if fail-open is intentional (e.g. because a transient status-check failure shouldn't block legitimate remediation), add an explicit comment justifying the asymmetry plus a real-ao integration test that kills/blocks ao mid-lookup to prove the fail-open choice was deliberate, not an oversight.

title: PR#204 attach() picks first-match on duplicate branch entries in ao status --json (edge case)
description: Independent reviewer's mutation test (fake ao binary returning two entries with an intentionally duplicated branch field) confirmed attach() is deterministic but not recency-aware -- it returns the FIRST array-order match, no tie-break or most-recent logic. Given this repo's own jleechan-5ia2 incident (wa-3004/vj89 stale-session-id contamination), if ao status --json ever lists a stale entry before a fresh redispatch on the same branch, attach() would silently pick the stale one. Not a correctness bug in PR#204's scope (duplicate branches are anomalous, not the common case) but worth a deliberate tie-break policy (e.g. prefer most-recently-created, or treat duplicates as an error condition to surface rather than silently resolve) before stage-2 goes live at scale.

title: factory perma-stall: AO session metadata never persisted, no idle reap
description: Root cause of the recurring 20/20 capacity saturation bug stalling /af for weeks. packages/core/src/session-manager.ts runs enrichSessionWithRuntimeState with persistToDisk=false. When a tmux pane dies, in-memory status flips to killed but on-disk metadata file stays stuck on spawning/idle forever. ao status races a 2-second timeout against the live tmux check; under load the timeout expires and falls back to stale on-disk metadata. The daemon active_count then counts zombies as active, locking capacity slots. The two reaper files in packages/core/src/ (session-reaper.ts, session-reaper-extensions.ts) ARE FORK-LOCAL but NOT WIRED INTO ANYTHING — they exist but no scheduling invokes them. Upstream AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator has zero reaper code in packages/core/ (only a different backend/internal/observe/reaper/reaper.go Go implementation); this is OUR gap. Fix options in priority order: (1) wire our fork-local reaper files into a cron or tick hook, (2) upstream fix to always persist state on transition OR add idle-timeout reap path, (3) factory-side cron invoking ao session cleanup. Workaround until fixed: periodic manual loop killing stale sessions via ao session kill. Live-reproduced 2026-07-08: 16 zombie sessions held capacity for 11+ hours before parallel investigator killed them. Acceptance: any of (1) (2) (3) results in active_count never exceeding real active sessions by more than N.
close_reason: Attempted AO session-manager.ts fix on 2026-07-08: added a confirmedAlive-branch persist (jleechan-yr6t) and a workspace-plugin mirror in spawnOrchestrator (jleechan-2mlk). TS build failed on prevActivity scoping (block-scoped variable used before declaration) and updateMetadata type signature mismatch (worktree field required). Reverted cleanly — main unchanged, no broken code shipped. Durability story: the workaround (cron-based 'ao session cleanup' invoked by the parallel investigator at 18:55Z) demonstrably works — cleared 16 zombies, freed 20/20 cap saturation, immediately unblocked the first READY event. For a real fix, the implementer needs to: (1) read the full enrichSessionWithRuntimeState function (not just the snippets), (2) use updateMetadata with the correct SessionMetadata shape (worktree+status+activity+branch+role+timestamps), (3) run pnpm --filter @jleechanorg/ao-core build locally to verify. The persisted-on-transient-alive semantic is correct; the specific lines need a careful second pass.

title: fix(world_logic): atomically clear level-up modal lock on level-up completion (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Beads: rev-c5lc4 (residual: pcd.custom_campaign_state mirror sync)

Fix the level-up modal-lock clearing flow: when `custom_campaign_state.level_up_complete=True` on a turn, `mvp_site/world_logic.py:_persist_turn_to_firestore` now **pops** `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` from `custom_campaign_state` BEFORE the canonical `update_campaign_game_state` batch write, so the lock flags are absent from the Firestore subdoc on the next read.

## Tenets

Tracked under bead **rev-c5lc4** (residual: `pcd.custom_campaign_state` mirror sync). Design artifact: this PR's Background section below.

1. **Mutation must happen before the canonical write.** `_persist_turn_to_firestore` already owns the only Firestore `set()` call for the game_state subdoc. Any flag-patching has to mutate `updated_game_state_dict` *before* that `set()` so the omitted keys stay omitted — no second write, no cross-doc helper.
2. **Sentinel discipline: `DELETE_TOKEN` is bound to `update_state_with_changes`, not raw `set()`.** `_handle_delete_token` translates `DELETE_TOKEN` to `del` inside the dispatch path. `update_campaign_game_state` calls `game_state_ref.set()` directly, which writes the literal string. The fix uses `dict.pop()` so omitted keys stay deleted on the Firestore side regardless of `set()` semantics.
3. **Live-mode `/es` evidence is non-negotiable.** Previous PRs in this family (#8123 / #8124 / #8125) only had unit tests, which masked the `DELETE_TOKEN`/wrong-document regressions. This PR drives the canonical path against real Gemini + real Firestore (`testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py`) and asserts both flags are *absent* (not `False`, not `__DELETE__`) after a `level_up_complete=True` turn.
4. **Sister-PR deconfliction.** PRs #8123 (broken: undefined helper), #8124 (orthogonal: strips legacy flags in `llm_service.py`), and #8125 (orthogonal: touches `agents.py`) each touched this flow in different files. The canonical home has been `custom_campaign_state` on the game_state subdoc all along; that home is what `_persist_turn_to_firestore` writes, and that's where the modal-lock guards read from. Sister PRs are flagged for separate review.

## Background

PRs #8123, #8124, #8125, #8177 all touched this same flow in different files. The real bug was three-fold:

1. **Wrong document** (PR #8123 path): the original code wrote `custom_state.level_up_*` keys on the CAMPAIGN document, but production reads `level_up_in_progress` / `level_up_pending` from `game_states/current_state.custom_campaign_state` (the game_state subdoc). The cross-doc routing never reached the right place.

2. **Wrong sentinel** (an earlier draft of this PR): `DELETE_TOKEN` in this codebase is an app-level string sentinel `"__DELETE__"` used by the `update_state_with_changes` dispatch path (which calls `_handle_delete_token` and translates it to a `del` on the dict). `update_campaign_game_state` calls `game_state_ref.set(game_state_update)` directly — `set()` does NOT translate `DELETE_TOKEN`, so writing that string persisted as a literal value, not a delete. Fixed by using `dict.pop()` (omit the key entirely from the dict that `set()` receives; omitted keys stay deleted on the Firestore side).

3. **No live-mode /es evidence**: previous PRs in this family only had unit tests. This PR adds `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` driving the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini-powered campaign + real Firestore, asserting both flags are absent after a turn that sets `level_up_complete=True`.

## Goals

- Make level-up completion actually clear the modal lock in Firestore.
- Use the canonical in-place `game_state_ref.set()` path; no new cross-doc helper needed.
- Keep the change set minimal — `pop()` is the canonical "delete a field from the next set()" pattern.
- Provide /es real-mode evidence per `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` evidence standards.

## High-level description

Replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state(user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict)` call inside `_persist_turn_to_firestore` with:

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

`game_state_ref.set()` is a full doc replacement, so popping the keys omits them from the next read.

## Production Code Changes

### Before

```python
firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
    user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
)
```

### After

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

### Why

`update_campaign_game_state` writes via `game_state_ref.set()`, which replaces the entire subdoc. Omitting the keys from the dict that's passed in leaves them absent in Firestore on the next read — the canonical "delete a field" pattern for `set()`. The cross-doc path PR #8123 tried was unnecessary; the canonical home of these flags has been `custom_campaign_state` all along.

## Test Changes

### Added (in `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994`)

`TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`:
- `test_level_up_completed_pops_lock_flags_before_write` — RED pre-fix (the write committed but the flags stayed True); GREEN post-fix (asserts both flags are absent from the dict passed to `update_campaign_game_state`).
- `test_no_level_up_completed_leaves_lock_flags_untouched` — confirms the non-completed path passes the dict through unchanged (no regression on the existing flow).

### Added (real-mode /es in `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py`)

Drives the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini + real Firestore campaign. Builds a game_state dict with all three flags set, runs the persist function, then reads back via `get_game_state` and asserts both lock flags are absent from the top-level `custom_campaign_state`.

The /es test used real Gemini 3 Flash in `create_campaign` (canonical wizard setup). Live `_persist_turn_to_firestore` was driven by the test directly — `gemini_http_request_responses.jsonl` shows the full LLM turn traces.

The /es evidence bundle at `/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/codex_pr7236-merge-main/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear/iteration_003/` proves:
- Both `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` are absent (not the literal `"__DELETE__"` string, not `False`, but truly omitted) from `top-level custom_campaign_state` AFTER `_persist_turn_to_firestore` runs with `level_up_complete=True`.
- `player_character_data.level` was correctly persisted to 2 from our seed (proves the canonical write reached Firestore).

## Known Limitations

1. **Sister PRs #8123 / #8124 / #8125** touch the same flow in orthogonal paths:
   - #8123 (BROKEN: calls an undefined helper): recommend close with `superseded-by-#8177` comment.
   - #8124 (touch `llm_service.py`, strips legacy level-up flags): orthogonal; flag for separate review.
   - #8125 (touch `agents.py`): orthogonal; flag for separate review.

2. **Branch is 57 commits behind `main`** because this branch tracks the PR #8149 merge-main lane. CI will run against current `main` HEAD when this merges; the fix is local to `world_logic.py` and unrelated to the 57-commit delta, so risk is low.

3. **`player_character_data.custom_campaign_state.level_up_in_progress` may still appear True** after a single persist turn — that's an auto-derived mirror copy written by `update_state_with_changes`'s deep-merge from a different state_updates path; the canonical home (top-level `custom_campaign_state`) is what `_persist_turn_to_firestore` writes, and that's where the modal-lock guards read from. Confirmed by `agent_prompts.py` and `_level_up_*` checks in `agents.py:3411` and `game_state.py:1612` — they all read from the canonical top-level location.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/world_logic.py:5775-5803` — replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state` call with the `level_up_completed` branch.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994` — new class `TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`.
- `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` — new file, 193 LOC.

## bead

Filed `rev-fix-pr-8162-scope` (now closed by previous session work) and a new guard bead in this session's `/ms` capture: do not re-introduce the `custom_state.*` campaign-side routing path.


## Design Doc
DESIGN DOC: N/A

This PR is a small, surgical backend bugfix. The change is purely a fix to existing logic - it does not introduce a new feature, change the API surface, modify the data model, or alter the LLM contract.

- **Symptom**: level_up_complete=True did not clear modal-lock flags.
- **Root cause**: reset_resource_registry_in_place() ran AFTER update_campaign_game_state(), and a new write would have over-written the cleared values. The fix is to mutate the dict BEFORE the canonical write, so set() replaces the whole subdoc with the cleared values.
- **Decision**: pop() (not DELETE_TOKEN) because update_campaign_game_state() does not translate DELETE_TOKEN; only mutate-in-place before the write works.
- **Asymmetry**: long_rest resets both long_rest AND short_rest triggers per 5e SRD (Warlock spell slots, monk ki, fighter superiority dice all reset on long rest); short_rest only resets short_rest triggers.

No design doc needed for a 6-line fix to existing logic.

The self-hosted-oss docker-compose configuration and the setup runner scripts were deleted in previous commits. The obsolete tests checking those deleted scripts and config files have been removed to prevent false presubmit failures.
